outcome: Bellmere retains its grief, borrowed dead and permanent fog. The Compact now has a fixed chronology, specific permissions and disclosed costs; the mystery has stable evidence, and the climax offers distinct, consequential routes.
publication: Published v1.0 Release Candidate as catalog revision 2; every field matches the reviewed source. The previous catalog entry was backed up. Existing campaigns keep their starting edition. Source commit is local; the shared-branch Git push awaits approval because unrelated location-display and test commits are ancestors.
changes: One annual Setting occurs at the recorded third-night high tide. Act One's occupied chair is a separate household supper; postponing dinner cannot change expiry.

Entries, face licenses, threshold invitations and life/name pledges are distinct. Reading or mentioning a name does not bind anyone. Civic renewal costs one voluntarily pledged year of life; Perce's ten-year rejuvenations are separate.

The dead clerk's handwriting, Guest access, Corentin's omissions, Hesper's false entry and Perce's receipts have fixed causes. Independent records preserve essential information when witnesses refuse or disappear.

Wick is the original living child, with a specific mistaken claim and remedy. Borrowed bodies leave salt husks and do not resurrect buried humans; the Guest's ultimate origin and moral self-understanding remain uncertain.

Ordinary renewal can lawfully omit all dead names. Negotiation can further limit the living giver's licensed face. Severance ends protection at the next tide, whereas nonrenewal keeps the current term until its fixed expiry. Departure and prepared evacuation can work; the permanent fog survives.
Pre-1.0 draft promoted to v1.0 Release Candidate after final review, with no story changes in that metadata promotion.
verification: Four immutable snapshots each received all fourteen perspectives. Actual normalization and isolated import preserved 69 authored fields, six NPCs, six locations, seven rules and nine arcs. Report links and desktop/mobile rendering were checked before shipment. The mandatory commit gate passed all standalone suites and 3,106 engine assertions. No narrated session, consent-recognition behavior or real-player test was run.
rounds: Baseline v0.01: the annual dinner occupied two positions in the timeline; naming, payment and exit rules were undefined; Wick and the dead-hand entry lacked fixed truths, and corpses conflicted with non-resurrection.

Round 1 v0.02: fixed the chronology, Compact, evidence and endings. Design/player reviews found two remaining ambiguities: early refusal versus early severance, and indoor invitation for a licensed living face. Writing lenses found no new material issue.

Round 2 v0.03: separated the clocks and defined living-face invitations. The player panel identified a lawful delisting route that made the purported negotiation benefit redundant; the design pass corroborated it.

Round 3 v0.04: explicitly honors ordinary delisting without Guest approval and reserves negotiation for further limits on the licensed face. All fourteen final assessments found no further required source edits. Final v1.0 promotion changes only version and status.
remaining: Ready for actual playtesting, not declared Released. Exercise ordinary name questions, explicit invitations, early refusal, early seal destruction, no-witness investigation, Wick's remedy, delisting before renewal, a rejected negotiation and evacuation. Confirm the narrator preserves permissions, costs and clocks rather than inventing new clauses after a choice. No duration claim.
